questions.q: In the chapter's per-user Isolation Forest baselines, what contamination parameter is used and what does it mean?
options: 0.02, meaning roughly 2% of sessions are expected to be anomalous
0.50, meaning half of sessions are expected to be anomalous
0.0001, meaning virtually no sessions are anomalous
1.0, meaning every session is scored as anomalous
questions.explain: The baseline builder sets contamination=0.02, explicitly expecting about 2% anomalous sessions since you never have a labeled set of known malicious sessions.

questions.q: The catalog reconnaissance detector flags a user/hour session when which thresholds are exceeded?
options: catalog_query_ratio > 5% or more than 2 distinct catalog objects
catalog_query_ratio > 10% or more than 5 distinct catalog objects
catalog_query_ratio > 50% or more than 25 distinct catalog objects
catalog_query_ratio > 20% or more than 10 distinct catalog objects probed
questions.explain: The chapter flags sessions where catalog queries exceed 20% of total queries or more than 10 distinct catalog objects (e.g., sys.tables, sys.database_principals) were probed, as a reconnaissance indicator.

questions.q: In the detection pipeline, what anomaly score cutoff decides which sessions go to the LLM classifier?
options: Scores below -1.0
Scores below -0.15
Scores above 0.0
Scores above 0.85
questions.explain: run_detection_pipeline uses anomaly_threshold=-0.15; Isolation Forest score_samples below this threshold mark anomalous sessions for LLM threat classification.

questions.q: In the chapter's MITRE ATT&CK mapping for SIEM export, which technique ID maps to DATA_EXFILTRATION?
options: T1078 (Valid Accounts)
T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application)
T1005 (Data from Local System)
T1486 (Data Encrypted for Impact)
questions.explain: The mitre_mapping dictionary maps 'DATA_EXFILTRATION' to 'T1005' (Data from Local System) in the CEF syslog events sent to the SIEM.

questions.q: For a CRITICAL-severity threat assessment, which automated responses does the chapter's routing map trigger?
options: Alert security, terminate the suspicious session, and emergency escalation (page)
Log to SIEM only
Send a low-priority email digest
Take no action until the next business day
questions.explain: SEVERITY_RESPONSE_MAP assigns CRITICAL: ALERT_SECURITY, TERMINATE_SESSION, EMERGENCY_ESCALATION — though the chapter requires governance like exempt service-account allowlists and dual-signal confirmation before termination.
